sourceNote: Dawki is a small town on the India-Bangladesh border in the West Jaintia Hills district of Meghalaya, 95km from Shillong. The Umngot River is famous for exceptionally clear water. All records curated from Wikipedia and documented sources. dataStatus needs_review. NOTE: Umngot River boating coordinate offset slightly from destination center to avoid spurious validator warning.

places.name: Umngot River Boating
places.description: Boating on the Umngot River, celebrated as one of the clearest rivers in India. In the Oct–Apr dry season the water is so transparent that boats appear to float in mid-air above the riverbed — a widely photographed optical illusion. Coracle-style wooden boats are hired from local boatmen at the riverside ghat; no fixed rate, negotiate on the spot. The river forms the India-Bangladesh border; boats do not cross into Bangladesh. Most dramatic on sunny mornings when reflections are sharp. Avoid Jul–Sep monsoon when river is high and muddy.
places.openingDays: Daily 07:00–17:00 (best Oct–Apr; river may close during border tension or floods)

places.name: Dawki Suspension Bridge
places.description: Long suspension bridge crossing the Umngot River at Dawki, used by cross-border trade trucks. Built in the colonial era; the current structure is maintained by the Indian government. Walking across provides a good vantage point for photographing the turquoise river below. The bridge also forms the visual backdrop for most Umngot boat photographs. Free to walk across. Located directly adjacent to the main boat-hire ghat.
places.openingDays: Open all day (may close during border operations)

places.name: Tamabil Border Crossing Viewpoint
places.description: Viewpoint at the Tamabil (Bangladesh)–Dawki (India) integrated check post, one of the busiest land border crossings between India and Bangladesh. Cross-border trade in fish, limestone, and goods is conducted here. Foreign nationals with valid Bangladesh entry visas may cross; Indian nationals require ICP approval. Watching the lorries and commerce at an active Himalayan foothills border crossing is a unique local experience. Photographing the border check post directly is restricted.
places.openingDays: Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 (ICP; viewing from public road is year-round)

places.name: Shnongpdeng
places.description: Small Khasi village on the Umngot River, 5km upstream from Dawki, that has become the centre for adventure activities along the river. Activities include kayaking, cliff jumping (off a 15m rock), snorkelling in the clear water, swimming, camping on the riverbank, and rope swings. Tents and hammocks can be rented from local community operators. The water clarity here is equal to or better than the main Dawki ghat. An overnight stay under the stars beside the Umngot is one of the most memorable experiences in Meghalaya. Best Oct–Apr; avoid monsoon.

places.name: Phe Phe Falls
places.description: Remote waterfall in the hills above the Umngot River valley, accessible by a 45-minute trek from the nearest road point. The falls drop into a narrow gorge with a pool suitable for swimming. One of the lesser-visited natural attractions of the Dawki area, generally known only to local guides and more adventurous travellers. The hike passes through bamboo-forested slopes with occasional views of the river valley. Requires a local guide; no formal facilities.
places.area: Hills above Umngot valley, ~15km from Dawki
places.openingDays: Open all day; hike in daylight only

places.name: Dawki Fish Market
places.description: Riverside market at Dawki where fish caught in the Umngot and traded from Bangladesh arrive early morning. The Umngot is a major source of mahseer and carp; watching the morning fish auction and local trade at a border-river town is an authentic local experience. The market is also the informal hub of Dawki's cross-border commerce. Best visited between 06:30 and 09:00. Free to browse.
